name: Smaller advisers

subjectOf.text: If the administrative and compliance costs created by Title IV disproportionally affect smaller hedge fund advisers, then over time smaller fund advisers could be forced out of the market or pushed to merge with other funds.
subjectOf.abstract: If the administrative and compliance costs created by Title IV should disproportionally affect smaller hedge fund advisers, it is conceivable that over time smaller fund advisers could get forced out of the market or merge with other funds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: conditional on the anecdotal evidence of a disproportionate effect being true

subjectOf.text: Based on these findings, there appears to be no immediate need for policy makers to address concerns over a possible effect of Title IV on startup hedge funds and smaller hedge fund advisers.
